data.name: Philippines
data.summary: The Philippines taxes foreigners, resident or not, only on Philippine-source income, so foreign dividends and gains on foreign securities are untaxed. Philippine dividends bear a 10% final tax, and listed Philippine shares a 0.1% tax on the sale price. Estate tax is a flat 6% above PHP 5 million, and for a resident alien it reaches the worldwide estate. Gifts above PHP 250,000 a year bear 6% donor's tax. There is no wealth tax. Residence is available through the Special Resident Retiree's Visa and other visas.

regimes.name: Resident alien
regimes.description: Aliens are taxed only on Philippine-source income; 6% estate tax on a resident's worldwide estate.
regimes.eligibility: A foreigner living in the Philippines with no definite intention as to length of stay is a resident alien; aliens staying more than 180 days a year on a fixed-term basis are non-resident aliens engaged in trade or business.

capital_gains.summary: Aliens, whether resident or not, are taxed only on Philippine-source income, so a foreign family's gains on foreign securities and foreign property are not taxed. Philippine-source gains: shares listed and traded on a stock exchange bear a stock transaction tax of 0.1% of the gross selling price (cut from 0.6% by the Capital Markets Efficiency Promotion Act, effective 2025); unlisted shares 15% of net gain; Philippine real property 6% of the higher of gross price and fair market value.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Foreign-source gains of aliens: outside the tax net.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: PwC's individual pages still show the 0.6% stock transaction tax; PwC's corporate 'Other taxes' page shows the 0.1% rate after the 2025 reform, which is used here. Philippine citizens who are resident are taxed on worldwide income (not relevant to EU/US/OTHER citizens).

sources.title: Philippines - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: The 0.1% stock transaction tax is from PwC's corporate page; the RA 12214 text was not opened.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Proceeds-based taxes converted to a rate on the gain assuming the gain is half the proceeds: listed shares 0.1% of proceeds -> 0.2%; Philippine real property 6% of gross price -> 12%. Unlisted Philippine shares 15% of net gain. Foreign assets 0 (aliens taxed on Philippine-source income only).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Dealers in securities are taxed on ordinary income at graduated rates (up to 35%).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Not taxed for aliens (resident or non-resident).

dividends.summary: Resident aliens pay a 10% final tax on dividends from domestic corporations. Foreign dividends are foreign-source income and not taxed for aliens; there is no foreign tax credit for aliens (PwC).

sources.title: Philippines - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic 10% final (resident aliens). Foreign 0: outside the scope of tax for aliens.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Dividends to non-resident aliens 20%/25% final, to non-resident foreign corporations 25% (15% with tax-sparing), reducible by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: About 44 DTAs including the US, the UK and major EU states (PwC list).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Domestic corporations pay 25% CIT (20% for small companies); a company structure is not assumed.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Real property tax up to 1% (provinces) or 2% (cities and Metro Manila municipalities) of assessed value plus 1% for the special education fund. Foreigners cannot own land (condominium units up to 40% of a project).

inheritance.summary: Estate tax is a flat 6% of the net estate (TRAIN Law, NIRC Sec. 84). For citizens and residents (including resident aliens) the gross estate covers property wherever situated, after a PHP 5 million standard deduction, the family home (up to PHP 10 million), debts and the surviving spouse's share of conjugal property. Non-resident aliens are taxed only on Philippine property. Donor's tax is also 6%, on gifts above PHP 250,000 a year.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: PHP 5,000,000 standard deduction per estate; family home deduction up to PHP 10,000,000; donor's tax exemption PHP 250,000 per calendar year.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Reciprocity exemption for intangible personal property of non-resident aliens (NIRC Sec. 104; not verified). Foreign estate tax is creditable.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 10963 (TRAIN Law), amending NIRC Secs. 84-86 (estate tax) and 98-99 (donor's tax)

inheritance.gift_tax: Donor's tax 6% on total gifts above PHP 250,000 in a calendar year, paid by the donor.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Included in the gross estate of a resident alien (Sec. 85, 'wherever situated'); credit for foreign estate tax (Sec. 86(D)).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Residence of the decedent decides: resident aliens worldwide, non-resident aliens Philippine assets only.

residency.tax_residency_test: Aliens: 'resident alien' if living in the Philippines with no definite intention as to length of stay; aliens staying more than 180 days in a calendar year are at least non-resident aliens engaged in trade or business. Both are taxed on Philippine-source income only.

routes.name: Special Resident Retiree's Visa (SRRV) and other permanent visas
routes.requirements: SRRV for applicants aged 50+ with a deposit (amount varies by option and age; not verified); quota immigrant and treaty-based permanent visas exist.

corporate.summary: 25% CIT on domestic corporations' worldwide income (20% for small corporations); 2% minimum corporate income tax on gross income from the fourth year.
corporate.special_zones: PEZA economic zones and CREATE/CREATE MORE incentives (not researched).

sources.title: Philippines - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens pay US tax on worldwide income; Philippine tax on their foreign income is nil. The 6% Philippine estate tax on a resident alien's worldwide estate is creditable against US estate tax only within foreign-tax-credit limits (no estate tax treaty).
open_questions: Whether a family on a retiree or other permanent visa is a 'resident alien' (worldwide estate tax) or a non-resident alien depends on intention; assumed resident.

income.name: Philippines

income_tax.summary: Residents pay graduated tax of 0% to 35% (2023 onward) on compensation income; non-resident aliens engaged in trade or business use the same rates. Self-employed individuals and professionals under PHP 3 million of receipts can elect an 8% tax on receipts above PHP 250,000 instead. Foreign employees' SSS and PhilHealth contributions are capped at about PHP 51,000 a year.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Rate and cap are a blended equivalent: PwC states the maximum annual social tax for a foreign employee (SSS + PhilHealth) is PHP 51,000 (2025); PHP 51,000 / PHP 1,200,000 = 4.25%. Consistent with SSS employee 5% of a monthly salary credit capped at PHP 35,000 (PHP 21,000 a year) plus PhilHealth at about 2.5% of income up to PHP 100,000 a month (PhilHealth rate not verified). Pag-IBIG no longer required of foreigners. Self-employed SSS/PhilHealth rates are higher and not verified; the same blended figure is used. 8% option: 8% of gross receipts above PHP 250,000 in lieu of graduated rates and percentage tax, if not VAT-registered and receipts within PHP 3 million. Check pass 2026-10-15: PwC confirms only the PHP 51,000 maximum and the end of Pag-IBIG for foreigners; Forvis Mazars confirms SSS at 15% (employee 5%, employer 10%) on a monthly salary credit of PHP 5,000-35,000 from 2025, but did not state the self-employed share; PhilHealth 5% premium with a PHP 100,000 income ceiling was seen only in a search summary of PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002, so the self-employed rate remains a placeholder equal to the employee blend.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Business owners pay local business taxes (not modelled).

sources.title: Philippines - Individual - Taxes on personal income
SSS contribution rates increased to 15% starting January 1, 2025 (Forvis Mazars)

open_questions: Self-employed SSS and PhilHealth contribution rates not confirmed from an official page; the self-employed rate reuses the employee blend (4.25%) and probably understates the burden.
PhilHealth premium (5%, ceiling PHP 100,000) not opened on a PhilHealth or PwC page.
Whether foreign nationals are in scope of the 8% option and personal exemption details not covered on the page.
Philippine 2026 rates assumed unchanged from 2023 schedule.

regimes.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Executive Order 86)
regimes.description: Remote-worker visa created by Executive Order No. 86 (24 April 2025). The order's text (Lawphil excerpt) requires proof of remote work and of sufficient income earned outside the Philippines, health insurance, no criminal record and no employment in the Philippines, with a stay of a maximum of one year and renewal possible. It sets no minimum income and says nothing about taxation: the BIR only helps study the programme and issue implementing guidelines. The claim that holders are not tax resident and exempt on foreign-employer pay appears only on a secondary site (thedigitalnomad.asia) with no citation, so no exemption is recorded. The order required DFA guidelines within 30 days and a pilot within 60 days of effectivity; that site's page (updated 30 July 2026) still says the visa is not launched, and the Bureau of Immigration's visa list shows no digital nomad visa.
regimes.duration_note: EO 86 s.3: stay up to a maximum of one year, renewable; renewal terms await the implementing guidelines (the secondary site claims 12 + 12 months).

sources.title: Philippines Digital Nomad Visa - Detailed Information
Executive Order No. 86, s. 2025 (Digital Nomad Visa)

open_questions: Whether applications are actually open and the final income threshold depend on DFA implementing guidelines, which were not found.
No official statement on income-tax treatment of holders; a Bureau of Internal Revenue issuance would be needed.

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Numbeo average 1-bedroom apartment in city centre, 730 entries from 76 contributors in 12 months (all city price data); range PHP 23,000-50,331.

rent_2bed_monthly.description: Bamboo Routes, article of 21 September 2026: current asking rent for a two-bedroom condo in Makati only (no BGC or Manila-wide 2-bedroom figure on the page). Single figure, no range; furnished status not stated. Asking rents, not signed leases.

costs.notes: No 2-bedroom figure (Numbeo 3-bedroom city centre PHP 119,667); Lamudi, Expatistan and Global Property Guide pages could not be read, so left null. Makati/BGC not separated.

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: Executive Order 86 (2025) created a Digital Nomad Visa (stay up to one year, renewable, proof of foreign income, no work for Philippine employers), but implementing guidelines and launch could not be confirmed and the Bureau of Immigration's visa list does not show it; until it is open, remote workers use visa-free entry with extensions. Skilled employees need a 9(g) pre-arranged employment visa and Alien Employment Permit through a Philippine employer (not researched in detail here).
open_questions: DNV launch status and income threshold unconfirmed (no DFA guidelines found).
